NOT PUBLISHED - ROOT CAUSE ESTABLISHED 09/09/26, and it is NOT what the 04/09 state said. A credential-injecting GIT PROXY sits in front of both github.com (git) and api.github.com (API), inside the CONNECT tunnel (TLS is re-terminated at the agent proxy, whose CA the session trusts). It DISCARDS any credential you supply and injects its own: a Claude Code GitHub App user-to-server token authenticated AS ollieleuthart (proved - api.github.com/user returns his account id 295091854, X-Oauth-Client-Id Iv23liqTIFEtdIu6Vn1r, 15000/hr). It then serves that credential ONLY for repos in 'this session's authorized repository set'. THAT SET IS EMPTY - anthropics/claude-code, octocat/Hello-World and torvalds/linux all 403 with the identical message, so ssa-tracker is not specifically excluded; NOTHING is attached. The git path says it outright: 'access denied by the git proxy: ollieleuthart/ssa-tracker is not in this session's authorized repository set, so the proxy will not inject a credential for it. To fix, add the repository to the session's sources.' CONSEQUENCES FOR FUTURE RUNS: (1) NEVER ask Ollie for a PAT - the proxy discards it, it cannot even be tested here, and the injected identity is already his. (2) 'Retry in a fresh session' only helps if that session has the repo ATTACHED AS A SOURCE at creation; a fresh session with nothing attached fails identically. (3) It is not an egress-policy block - the agent proxy's recentRelayFailures shows ZERO github entries (only google hosts from the Playwright run), the CONNECT succeeds, and the 403 body carries no Server or X-GitHub-Request-Id header, unlike the genuine 200 from /user. WHY IT STARTED: pushing worked continuously from 19/06/26 to 01/09/26 13:33 AEST (commit 3cec7b2, the current HEAD, which is byte-identical to the deployed index.html). Every commit in the repo's history is authored AND committed as 'ssa <ollie@smart-switchappliances.com>' in near-simultaneous pairs one second apart - the signature of the Contents API method with an explicit committer, using Ollie's own PAT. That is NOT the GitHub App identity, so before 01/09 api.github.com was an ordinary host and his PAT reached GitHub. The proxy interception appeared between 01/09 and 04/09. Nothing about the repo, the token or the tracker changed - the session type did.
